issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch short-circuits and skips valid checks when url() is present in params.
issues.detail: The guard `if (primary === 'url' && /url\(/i.test(params)) return;` exits the function for the case the rule is meant to validate, silently bypassing downstream diagnostics on malformed or non-standard params containing url(). Hickey and Dijkstra both flag the inverted logic; mirror the 'string' branch and skip only when there is nothing to check.

issues.description: font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC regexes have undocumented case-sensitivity asymmetry and miss mixed-value cases.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED uses /i while HAS_NUMERIC is case-sensitive with no stated invariant. Worse, the 'numeric' fast path returns when no named keyword is present, conflating 'contains a keyword' with 'is named' — a mixed value like '400 bold' is misclassified. State the predicate explicitly and align the flags.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE omits the /i flag that HAS_KEYWORD uses with no stated invariant.
issues.detail: The asymmetric flag set is unjustified in code or comment. Percentages are digits so case is irrelevant for the literal, but the inconsistency reads as an oversight to the next maintainer. Pick one stance and document the precondition.

issues.description: Using `/./` as a 'match everything' sentinel for walkRules is clever-where-obvious would do.
issues.detail: walkRules already treats undefined as 'walk everything'. Branching on whether a filter exists and calling walkRules(filter, cb) or walkRules(cb) separates data from regex semantics and reads cleanly. Same generated work, smaller surface for the next reader.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE / HAS_NAMED regexes are built by joining keyword sets without escaping.
issues.detail: The construction silently assumes every token in the source Set is regex-safe. Today the contents are alphabetic or digits plus '%', so it works; tomorrow a metacharacter would change meaning without erroring. Escape at the join or annotate the precondition.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation pre-filter `/:/` is too permissive to deliver real perf gain.
issues.detail: The regex matches every pseudo-class, attribute selector with a colon, and namespace prefix — not just pseudo-element candidates. The move is consistent with sibling selector-* rules but the perf benefit is marginal. Either narrow to `/::?[a-z]/i` or note that this is for consistency, not speed.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a sound, well-scoped perf patch: cheap regex prefilters before expensive parser walks across six *-notation rules. Two correctness concerns are consensus blockers — the import-notation 'url' branch returns in the wrong direction and the font-weight-notation guard misreads mixed values. Several taste issues recur: unescaped keyword-joined regexes, undocumented case-sensitivity asymmetries, and a `/./` sentinel where undefined would do. Lands after the P1 fixes; the pattern would benefit from being lifted into a shared option-to-prefilter table rather than reinvented per rule.
